exposure: MRI patterns (basal ganglia/thalamus involvement, watershed lesions)
cohort: Forty inborn term neonates diagnosed with moderate to severe hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) based on clinical and MRI findings, admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit.
finding: The study highlights the complex interplay of maternal, intrapartum, and neonatal factors in the development and outcomes of HIE, emphasizing the importance of identifying early risk factors; no significant associations were found between MRI patterns and muscle tone or seizure activity at discharge.
mod_finding: 27 (67.5%) of the neonates with HIE were delivered by cesarean section; no specific association between mode of birth and reported outcomes (muscle tone, seizure activity) was mentioned.
birth_weight: Primarily term neonates; 75% of the cohort had a birth weight <2.5 kg.
